newsitem.title: USA: Man found innocent of shooting N.Y. cop.
newsitem.headline: Man found innocent of shooting N.Y. cop.

text.p: A New York jury said Thursday that they acquitted a man accused of allegedly shooting a police officer because it was a case of mistaken identity.
It took the jury less than three hours to find Jose Urena, 23, from the Dominican Republic, innocent after a trial at Manhattan Supreme Court.
"The biggest problem with the case was the description given by the officer of the man he said shot him. It didn't even come close to the man who was on trial," said juror Robert Turner.
Urena, who was accused of attempted murder and gun possession charges, had faced 25 years in prison. Until his arrest in June 1996, he had no arrest record.

Police Officer Andrew DeStefano, a seven-year veteran, told the jury Wednesday that he was on routine patrol in the Washington Heights section of upper Manhattan when he spotted Urena acting suspiciously. When he tried to question him, Urena allegedly pulled out a silver pistol and shot.
When the .25-calibre bullet hit his bulletproof vest, it felt "like a baseball bat across the ribs," he said.
DeStefano initially described the gunman as 5-feet-10 and 180 pounds. Urena is 6-feet-2 and weighs 220 pounds.
DeStefano also misidentified Urena in the lineup.
"There was a lot of pressure on the Police Department to get somebody," Turner added.

Other jurors concurred, saying the primary witnesses against Urena was a paid confidential informant and a homeless man. During the trial, it came out that when he went to identify the suspect in a police lineup, he "reeked of alcohol."
